text: Add leakage-safe request-context categorical fields tab, hour, and weekday to the five-field FM baseline.
rationale: This is the highest-evidence candidate: the train-only temporal screen found request context was the only feature group with positive aggregate primary lift (+0.00221), positive lift on all four screened days, and 100% coverage. Downside risks: the daily primary standard deviation (0.00580) exceeds the aggregate lift, so the official gain may be noisy or absent; added context can also overfit short-lived temporal correlations.
exact_ablation: Add exactly three train-vocabulary categorical FM fields—tab, hour derived from impression time, and weekday derived from impression date—while leaving the FM architecture, loss, optimizer, seed, and all existing five fields unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.002 to +0.005 from better within-user contextual ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.004 from placing context-appropriate items nearer the top five.

text: Add only the tab request-context field to the five-field FM baseline.
rationale: Tab is a pre-ranking request-context signal contained in the only feature family with a positive, four-day-positive temporal-screen lift. This narrow ablation isolates whether the existing tab field is the useful part of the bundle. Downside risks: tab may already be weakly represented through item exposure patterns, and a single context field may not produce enough score variation to improve nDCG@5.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one categorical FM field for tab; retain all seed-model fields and all training settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.003, with a small improvement if tab changes item preference within a user.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.002, with limited top-five benefit expected from tab alone.

text: Add only an hour-of-day request-context field to the five-field FM baseline.
rationale: The positive screen result for request context includes hour and was positive on each screened temporal day, making hour a plausible compact temporal-preference signal. Downside risks: hour effects may be nonstationary across the official validation week and coarse hourly buckets may dilute minute-level behavior; it can improve aggregate ordering without moving positives into the top five.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one categorical FM field for impression hour derived from the logged request time; change no other field, model, loss, or training parameter.

expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.002 through modest top-rank context matching.

text: Add only a weekday request-context field to the five-field FM baseline.
rationale: Weekday is included in the sole positive screened request-context family and is deterministically available at impression time. It is a cheap test of weekly consumption rhythm without adding multiple fields. Downside risks: only a limited number of weekdays appear in the training period, so estimates may be sparse and validation-week behavior may differ; weekday may mainly affect calibration rather than within-user rank.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one categorical FM field for weekday derived from impression date; leave every other baseline component unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: 0.000 to +0.002, likely smaller than the complete context bundle.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.001, with little expected direct top-five movement.

text: Add a single joint tab-by-hour request-context token to the five-field FM baseline.
rationale: The measured positive request-context bundle suggests that context interactions may matter rather than independent main effects. A joint token directly represents tab-specific time-of-day preference while remaining available before ranking. Downside risks: the joint vocabulary is substantially sparser than separate fields, unseen combinations require an unknown bucket, and sparse interactions can reduce both GAUC and nDCG@5 under temporal drift.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one categorical FM field whose value is the concatenated tab-by-hour token; do not add separate tab, hour, or weekday fields.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 if tab-dependent hourly preferences generalize.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003 if the interaction improves top-five discrimination.

text: Replace binary cross-entropy with positive-class-weighted binary cross-entropy in the seed FM.
rationale: The official objective gives substantial importance to positive ordering, and the available request-context screen establishes that ranking-relevant signal exists beyond IDs. Increasing positive gradient weight may make the FM exploit such signal more strongly. Downside risks: class weighting can mostly shift score calibration, which need not improve within-user order; it may over-promote broadly positive items and harm GAUC or nDCG@5.
exact_ablation: Replace the unweighted binary cross-entropy training loss with one fixed positive-class-weighted binary cross-entropy loss, leaving features, architecture, optimizer, and epoch selection unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002, with possible degradation if weighting distorts pairwise order.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.003 if additional positive emphasis promotes relevant top-five items.

text: Replace binary cross-entropy with a within-batch pairwise logistic ranking loss in the seed FM.
rationale: GAUC is explicitly a within-user positive-negative ordering metric, so a pairwise objective is better aligned with the ranking mechanism than row-wise classification. The request-context screen demonstrates a small ranking-relevant signal that could benefit from stronger ordering alignment. Downside risks: batches can contain few valid same-user positive-negative pairs, reducing effective sample size; optimizing GAUC-like pairs may trade off against nDCG@5 and adds implementation complexity.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed binary cross-entropy loss with a within-user positive-negative pairwise logistic loss computed only from pairs present in each training batch; retain the seed features and FM architecture.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 from direct positive-negative ordering optimization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002 because pairwise optimization does not specifically emphasize rank five.

text: Increase the FM interaction embedding dimension from 16 to 32.
rationale: The positive request-context finding indicates that interaction capacity may be useful once context-dependent preferences are represented by the baseline's sparse IDs and fields. A dimension-only increase is a clean capacity test. Downside risks: the seed has no measured score, so there is no evidence that it is underfit; extra capacity can memorize sparse IDs, worsen temporal generalization, and increase runtime.
exact_ablation: Change only interaction_dimension from 16 to 32 in the existing FM configuration.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002, depending on whether current latent interactions are underfit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002, with possible small gains from sharper item ordering.

text: Decrease the FM interaction embedding dimension from 16 to 8.
rationale: The weak and variable context-screen effect cautions against excess sparse-model capacity; reducing dimension is a concrete regularization test for temporal robustness. Downside risks: reduced capacity can underfit user-item interactions and lower both metrics, particularly nDCG@5 where fine-grained score separation matters; no measured baseline overfitting diagnosis is available.
exact_ablation: Change only interaction_dimension from 16 to 8 in the existing FM configuration.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.001, with a modest upside only if the seed is overfit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.003 to +0.001, with top-five ordering at risk from underfitting.

text: Increase FM L2 regularization from 1e-6 to 1e-5.
rationale: Temporal-screen gains are modest relative to daily variation, making generalization control relevant before investing in broader feature expansion. This is a single interpretable regularization change. Downside risks: there is no measured evidence of seed overfitting, and stronger shrinkage can suppress useful user-item interactions, reducing both GAUC and nDCG@5.
exact_ablation: Change only the FM L2 coefficient from 0.000001 to 0.00001.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.001, with upside only through reduced temporal overfit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.002 to +0.001, as excessive shrinkage can flatten top-five scores.

text: Use a frequency-thresholded unknown bucket for rare training user and video IDs in the seed FM.
rationale: The positive context screen has full coverage, whereas sparse entity representations can be fragile under temporal shift. Collapsing rare IDs is a targeted representation regularizer that may allow shared context and item signals to generalize. Downside risks: frequency thresholding discards personalized signal for low-frequency entities and can materially hurt warm-user GAUC and nDCG@5; the threshold itself must be fitted on training rows only.
exact_ablation: Map training user_id and video_id values occurring fewer than a fixed training-only frequency threshold to their respective unknown buckets; keep all other fields and model settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.002, balancing less sparse memorization against lost personalization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.002 to +0.002, with potential top-five degradation for repeat users.

text: Add a single binary train-seen-video indicator field to the five-field FM baseline.
rationale: The supplied split inventory documents distinct temporal train and validation periods, so an explicitly train-fitted seen-item flag is a leakage-safe way to let the model distinguish known from unknown item representations. The request-context screen's full coverage provides a stable comparison setting. Downside risks: the cold-item screen contains only eight rows, so there is insufficient evidence that cold status matters; the flag may simply reinforce popularity or have negligible within-user ranking effect.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one binary FM field indicating whether the impression's video_id appeared at least once in the training split; construct the set from training data only.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002, with benefit if seen-status calibrates uncertain item embeddings.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002, with uncertain impact because cold-item support is extremely small.
